reason: E1 strongly supports the strength-ductility benefit of coherent nanoprecipitates in W-HEAs, but none of the cited evidence addresses the critical premise that such precipitates improve thermal conductivity or that the proposed annealing treatment achieves them in WTaCrV. E2 and E3 are about different alloys or irradiation resistance, not thermal transport.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates in W-based HEAs can simultaneously enhance strength and ductility by relieving stress concentrations.
Controlled annealing can induce coherent nanoprecipitates in a W-based HEA without deleterious phase coarsening.
Coherent interfaces reduce interfacial thermal resistance and improve heat carrier transmission.
The proposed WTaCrV alloy is microstructurally stable and resistant to irradiation-induced defects under relevant conditions.
The baseline as-cast alloy has poor thermal conductivity due to phonon scattering at incoherent interfaces.
